To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the quality of life of the informal caregivers of Alzheimer's patients is significantly associated with their health status, their level of care, and the presence of a secondary caregiver.

informal caregivers of Alzheimer patients are a heterogeneous group, and the most important variables associated with their health-related quality of life are their own physical health, the amount of rest periods, and the presence of another caregiver.
the EQ 5D dimensions with the highest level of severity were anxiety/depression and pain/discomfort.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact on caregivers of caring for people with Alzheimer's disease.

the relationship between the quality of life of informal caregivers of people with Alzheimer's disease and the characteristics of the disease, the characteristics of care, and the health status of the patient and the caregiver.
the relationship between informal care and the quality of life (QOL) of caregivers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no single, simple answer to the question of whether or not informal carers of people with dementia are at increased risk of developing dementia.
the quality of life of the caregiver is affected by the severity of the disease, the duration of care and the caregiver’s age and sex.

the quality of life of informal carers of people with AD is lower than that of the general population and the main determinants of this lower quality of life are the physical and psychological health of carers and the time devoted to care.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the results of this study show that the quality of life of the caregivers of Alzheimer's patients is affected by the care burden and by the physical and mental health of the caregiver.
we have shown that the quality of life of caregivers is affected by the disease and the care provided.
the main objective of the study was to assess the impact of informal caregiving on the quality of life of the caregivers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, despite the limitations in the literature and in the study, the EQ 5D is a useful tool to measure the quality of life in informal caregivers.

the EQ 5D is a valid and useful measure of the health-related quality of life (HRQoL) in caregivers of patients with dementia, especially for the anxiety/depression dimension, and that this dimension is the most relevant in determining the HRQoL of caregivers.
, despite the fact that the majority of patients and families in our sample had a good quality of life, the burden of caregiving was significant.
